[[Category:Glasgow Name Study]]
== Biography ==
William Glasgow of Larne died on '''5 October 1816, aged 53''', according to the published family monument, placing his birth about '''1763'''. His wife [[Stewart-72380|Elizabeth]] died on 17 September 1832, aged 60. Their monument names daughters [[Glasgow-3987|Jane Shutter]], [[Glasgow-3988|Eliza]] and [[Glasgow-3989|Mary]].<ref name="Monument">"Armorial Sculptured Stones of the County Antrim," ''Ulster Journal of Archaeology'', second series, vol. 6 (1900), p. 47, Glasgow inscriptions; [https://archive.org/details/ulsterjournalofa06ulstiala/page/47/mode/1up page image].</ref>

He was probably the son of [[Glasgow-1509|James Glasgow]] and [[Shutter-46|Janet Shutter]], as reported by the derivative family chronology. The distinctive name Jane Shutter supports that reconstruction, but William's original baptism or his surviving will must be read before treating the parentage as proved.


== Research Notes ==
Grant of probate of will of William Glasgow, Larne, Co. Antrim and copy will dated 6 December 1815.<ref>Repository :	Public Record Office for Northern Ireland
PRONI Reference :	D300/1/5/49</ref>

15. William3 Glasgow, b. 1763, 6. 1816, m. Elizabeth, had daughters Jane, Eliza and Mary. Buried St. Cedma's Cemetery in Larne. This could be the William Glasgow, captain of the "William," advertised in the Belfast News Letter 1792-1799. This occupational identification is an unverified suggestion from the inherited chronology; no inspected record connects the captain to this household. 

=== Jane Stewart estate connection, 1823 ===

An assignment of mortgage dated 8 November 1823 names '''Elizabeth Glasgow of Larne, widow, administratrix of Jane Stewart late of Curran, County Antrim, deceased'''. She assigned the mortgage interest to Roger Brown Curry, a Royal Navy lieutenant. The premises were a tenement and garden on the south side of New Town, Larne, 21 feet in front and 189 feet deep, bounded east by the lane to Larne Quay and west by James Mitchell's tenement. William Walsh McNeill, attorney, and James Glasgow, writing clerk, both of Larne, witnessed the assignment.<ref name="Estate1823">Registry of Deeds, memorial 548257, p. 522, assignment of mortgage dated 8 November 1823, registered 17 May 1826; [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSJ7-9935-Y FamilySearch image 359]. Original image inspected 21 September 2026.</ref>

This widow is a strong candidate for William Glasgow's widow Elizabeth, who survived him from 1816 until 1832, but the deed does not name her late husband. It establishes her authority to administer Jane Stewart's estate, without stating their relationship. The writing clerk's relationship to Elizabeth is also unstated. Jane's administration and the recited mortgage are specific sources to seek next; neither a parent nor a sibling should be assigned from the office of administratrix alone.

=== Original advertisements for the possible captain ===

The Northern Star names Wm. Glasgow as master of the brig William in advertisements for voyages from Belfast to Oporto in July 1792 and Bordeaux in December 1792.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/72015499/ Northern Star, 28 July 1792, p.1].</ref><ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/72017846/ Northern Star, 12 December 1792, p.1].</ref> These inspected notices substantiate the existence of the same-name captain mentioned in the family chronology, but they do not give his family or a Larne residence. Identification with this William remains unproved; the 1815 will is the next useful test.

=== Possible Captain Glasgow, brig Ann and Larne passenger reports, 1788 ===
The brig Ann is listed inward with Glasgow as master and Larne as origin.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/604128637/ The Columbian Herald, or, The Independent Courier of North-America, 1788-01-28, p.2].</ref>

The brig Ann, Captain Glasgow, is reported arriving from Larne after a tedious passage with near 200 passengers in good health; the report praises the captain’s humane and generous behaviour.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/1034014648/ The Pennsylvania Journal, or, Weekly Advertiser, 1788-02-13, p.2].</ref><ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/39957255/ The Independent Gazetteer, 1788-02-16, p.2].</ref>

The brig Ann is listed cleared out with Glasgow as master and Georgetown as destination.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/604128661/ The Columbian Herald, or, The Independent Courier of North-America, 1788-02-18, p.2].</ref>

The passenger reports repeat one notice. The inward and outward entries may concern the same captain, but none gives his forename or family; Larne is the voyage origin, not a recorded birthplace.

This may concern [[Glasgow-3324]]. Uncertain 1763 Larne birth and 1816 death permit 1788. Prior research compares this profile with the independently named 1792 William master; neither the Ann notices nor that later role identifies the 1788 captain.

=== Possible William Glasgow, Falmouth master, 1787 ===
William Glasgow is named as master of the Falmouth, from Baltimore, in an Amsterdam-arrivals entry dated 10 June 1787, printed in a newspaper issue of 6 May 1788.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/1034014372/ Poulson’s American Daily Advertiser, 1788-05-06, p.3].</ref>

The unusually late publication date is preserved: the shipping entry itself says 10 June 1787, although the issue is dated 6 May 1788. Baltimore and Amsterdam are voyage places, not proof of the master’s origin or kinship.

This may concern [[Glasgow-3324]]. Name and adult maritime chronology fit; Larne and the Belfast brig William are not stated in this Falmouth record.

=== Further shipping evidence, 1792–1797 ===

Additional advertisements in April and May 1792 explicitly name William Glasgow as master of the brig William for Rotterdam and return voyages; other named-master advertisements concern Oporto and Bordeaux. Surname-only arrival and cargo notices continue the William/Captain Glasgow trading sequence through 1796–1797, with probable rather than proved continuity. A February 1793 report describes departure from Bordeaux immediately before an embargo; it does not prove that the ship was captured or detained. Distinct notices name William Glasgow as master of the Jean in 1793 and 1794, including a safe arrival at Derry from London. Jean and William are different vessels, with compatible but unproved continuity of master. Several apparent advertisement/issue-date conflicts arise from the Northern Star’s printed issue ranges; the printed range and notice date should retain their separate meanings. Voyage ports and merchant addresses are not personal residence or family evidence.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/72014483/ Northern Star, 21 April 1792, The captain remains a compatible identification with William of Larne, supported by age, coastal locality and the inherited occupational suggestion. No advertisement names his wife or a personal Larne residence. The named master of the Jean may be the same man, but the vessel names do not prove it. The will dated 6 December 1815 remains the useful family-and-occupation test.
